title: Agent Feedback Architecture and CI Discipline
owner_directive: Upgrade OPS3 to OPS4 using the verified CI/AI-agent research and the reproduced Multiversal failure mode: stop CI overhandling, over-polling, browser-stalling remote-REPL behavior while preserving exact-head acceptance, multi-lane safety and truthful evidence.
reproduced_failure: During CWKS-10, the executor repeatedly expanded workflow/job/log inspection and used remote CI to discover development failures that should have been resolved in a smaller feedback loop.
Repeated status observation and per-platform handling increased tool volume and contributed to browser/session freezes without proportional material progress.
OPS3 already prohibited polling and overinstrumentation, but it did not make the pre-CI development/acceptance boundary and retry budget executable enough to prevent the behavior.
research_basis: DORA continuous-integration and small-batch guidance: fast feedback, small changes, and separation of quick validation from longer comprehensive gates.

OpenAI harness-engineering experience: agent productivity depends on strong local/worktree feedback loops, standard development tools, enforceable invariants and short-lived/small work units rather than ever-growing instruction manuals.

GitHub coding-agent guidance: agents should build/test/validate inside their development environment before producing mergeable candidates; concurrency controls should prevent stale validation work from wasting capacity.
Google large-scale testing research: pre-submit fast validation and prioritized testing reduce latency; exhaustive long feedback loops create developer friction.
Recent agent-testing research: agent-written tests can overuse mocks or optimize to visible tests, so real-boundary acceptance should include independent or cross-boundary evidence.
decisions: Preserve OPS3 authority, lane isolation, milestone receipts, exact-head publication, no-polling, failure-first diagnosis and small-context principles as OPS4 foundations.
Separate Tier-1 focused executable feedback from Tier-2 immutable remote candidate acceptance and Tier-3 terminal/comprehensive acceptance.

Focused validation is required when capable; if unavailable, the executor records concrete capability evidence and gets one bounded remote preflight rather than pretending the check was skipped or green.
Product/configuration failure kills that candidate head for acceptance. Another remote run requires a changed head and causal repair evidence.
Transient infrastructure failure receives at most one same-head retry with concrete infrastructure evidence. Repeated infrastructure failure requires a changed executor/runner/configuration path.
A suspected flaky test receives at most one classification rerun and cannot certify success while unresolved.
Real network/storage/process/auth/persistence/filesystem/installed/cross-platform requirements cannot be certified solely by same-agent mocks/unit tests.
Existing ops3-lane-state/* and ops3-publication-queue/* durable names remain compatibility identifiers during OPS4; renaming them is explicitly out of scope.
completion_rule: OPS4 is complete when the canonical door/contract/CURRENT/LANES/registry and validation workflow identify OPS4, the agent/CI feedback guard rejects skipped preflight, same-head product retries, duplicate active runs, exhausted infrastructure retries and mock-only real-boundary proof, inherited OPS3 safety regressions remain green, and no persistent product-lane selection is reset or silently changed.
next_action: Resume the already-authorized product lanes under OPS4. CWKS-10 remains in progress; GPR PCV-03F remains independently in progress; MTLC-02 remains selected_not_started until a future owner execution command.
